02-design-a.tex.fix: At first use write "the shifter view, the page the person on shift watches".

The second is the background host and runs the projector and the trend rollup. The third is the shifter host and runs the shifter view. Staging is therefore five machines: two workers and three storage nodes."

02-design-a.tex.quote: The chain to the catalog has four stages: stamp, buckets, audits, rules.
02-design-a.tex.problem: "The catalog" is never defined; it first appears as "the catalog maintenance" in a bare component list, so the reader does not know what is being maintained.
02-design-a.tex.source: docs/TEMPLATES_FIX_PLAN.md:209 (the catalog holds one definition document per template version, with labels attached to a version); briefs/walkthroughs-6-9.md:73 — "one check document per family into the catalog"
02-design-a.tex.fix: Define it here: "The catalog is one index holding one document per template the farm has ever seen, plus the results of the checks below."

02-design-a.tex.quote: \item The stamper, over a local socket, sets a template version and status and hands the chunk back.
02-design-a.tex.problem: "A template version" is never defined; the reader is told what a template is but not that a template changes over time, so every per-version count and the cover relation are unreadable.

02-design-a.tex.fix: In 02-design-a.tex:67, after the template definition: "A template widens as the miner sees more lines: a word that was fixed becomes a wildcard. Each state of a template is one version, and a version is what a record carries."

02-design-a.tex.quote: Version W covers version N when they share a family and a token count and W has, at every position, a wildcard or N's token.
02-design-a.tex.problem: A bare formal definition with no goal before it, so the reader cannot tell whether the cover relation is a search feature, a storage rule or a maintenance check.
02-design-a.tex.source: docs/TEMPLATES_FIX_PLAN.md:54 — "Search expansion by the cover relation, computed in the Shifter. 02-design-a.tex.fix: Goal first: "One search for a template must find the records stamped with its older, narrower versions. A wider version covers a narrower one when they share a family and a token count and the wider has, at every position, a wildcard or the narrower's token. That relation groups a template's versions, so no separate identifier is stored."

02-design-a.tex.fix: In all three places write "of the O2 process tree": "On staging 96.94~\% of the O2 process tree stayed on its worker."

02-design-a.tex.quote: \item The collector also posts the record to the shifter view's live lane, which holds the last 500 records.

02-design-a.tex.source: reports/inputs/dataflow-atlas.md:22 (audited) — "The same stamped record is also posted over HTTP to the live lane inside the Shifter on node-05. The Shifter keeps it in memory and streams it to every open browser over Server-Sent Events, with no cluster query at all."

02-design-a.tex.quote: A placement setting pins the index to its worker, so no byte crosses the network.
02-design-a.tex.problem: Walkthrough 2 is three sentences and never says who reads a local line, how one search reaches 200 workers, or what fanout costs; Section 4 then uses "fanout" as if it had been introduced.

Federated search: ask once, every node answers, the cost of fanout, and why the live lane exists so that the cluster is asked only when it must be."

The cluster asks every node that holds a shard of the pattern and merges the answers, so a search over all workers is as slow as the slowest worker. That is why the live lane exists: the everyday question, what is arriving now, never asks the cluster at all."

02-design-a.tex.quote: The control host runs Dashboards, the poller, the roster, the catalog maintenance, Alertmanager and the receiver.

02-design-a.tex.quote: The collector reads the five log sources, with the stamper beside it.

02-design-a.tex.fix: "In the target design the worker tier runs on every EPN; today it runs on three. It has four parts."

03-design-b.tex.problem: As written a disk at 95 % both pages and warns; the warn rule fires above 85 and at most 92, so the two rules do not overlap.

03-design-b.tex.fix: "... and reads the roster: one document naming every collector that must be running."

03-design-b.tex.problem: The rollup, "re-rolls", "closed buckets" and "settle" all arrive undefined, and the sentence carries three ideas.

03-design-b.tex.fix: "Seventeen detectors run, one for each watched thing: a host, a log family or an index. A silent host scores zero."

03-design-b.tex.problem: A comma splices two clauses, and the grade has no scale, so 0.5 and 0.7 carry no meaning.

03-design-b.tex.fix: "A detector grades every window from 0 to 1. A grade above 0.5 opens an episode. The monitor that pages on grades needs 0.7."

03-design-b.tex.quote: 17 detectors run, one per entity, and a silent host scores zero.
03-design-b.tex.problem: "Entity" is never defined, yet it shapes the whole alerting chain — one detector per entity, one episode per entity, a trend rule on an entity's share of the fleet.

03-design-b.tex.fix: "17 detectors run, one per entity: one machine, or one log family on one machine — the thing a rule is about."

03-design-b.tex.problem: Dashboards and Discover are product screen names used as plain nouns; neither is ever said to be the store's web interface and its search screen, and Dashboards first appears two sections earlier with no gloss.

03-design-b.tex.fix: At first use: "Dashboards, the store's own web interface, and inside it Discover, its search screen."

03-design-b.tex.problem: The reader is given the model's proper name and its schedule but not what it does or what a grade measures.

03-design-b.tex.problem: "Bucket" already means a five-minute template count document in Section 3.5; here it means a ten-minute slice of the trend rollup, and "re-rolls" and "closed" are new words used without definition.

03-design-b.tex.fix: Define the trend bucket at first use as "one ten-minute slice of counts per family and host", and say the rollup recomputes the last three slices once they can no longer receive late records.

03-design-b.tex.fix: Define at first use — "the fleet, every worker on the roster" — and write "one row per rostered collector" instead of "fleet document".

05-eval-a.tex.fix: "One single-threaded loop does 89.3~\% of the collector's processor work, so adding threads adds coordination and no throughput."

05-eval-a.tex.quote: A 47-cell re-run left one product change, the flush interval of Section~\ref{sec:eval-collector}.
05-eval-a.tex.problem: "Cell", "arm" and "round" are the report's private words for the shape of a measurement campaign, and none of the three is defined.
05-eval-a.tex.source: briefs/soak-index.md:17 — "A 47-cell re-run on 27 August at 5,000 a second replaced them and left one product change"; :15 — "The instrument failed four times before any arm ran."
05-eval-a.tex.fix: Define both in §5.1: "An arm is one setting under test. A cell is one arm at one rate, run three times."
